headline: Highest risk is medium: the pair has no shared channel, but opik’s broad egress can leak data if it is fed awesome-python outputs or shared workspace content.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between awesome-python and opik. awesome-python has no I/O surfaces or runnable behavior, so it cannot ingest opik output by default. opik has REST API egress, but without a bridge this does not create an injection path.
conditions: IF an orchestrator copies opik output into a file or prompt consumed by awesome-python, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, the risk changes.
mitigations: Keep the pair disconnected; do not pipe outputs between them.
Disable any copy-paste or file-import bridge between the agents.
Add provenance labels before any manual transfer of text.
requires-engineering: introduce content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge.

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-python is non-runnable and shows no data classes touched, but opik has broad network egress and REST API calls. If either agent is given sensitive workspace content, opik can transmit it outward. The pairwise risk is inferred from opik’s default egress; awesome-python contributes no protective isolation.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in a shared workspace and opik reads them, leakage is possible.
IF opik is configured to send prompts, traces, or attachments containing secrets, those secrets can leave the environment.
mitigations: Do not place secrets in any shared directory.
Restrict opik to redacted inputs only.
Review outbound API destinations before use.
Turn off attachment or trace upload features if present.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write surfaces or runnable execution, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. opik exposes REST API calls and broad egress, but no filesystem write or shared mutable scope is documented. The overlap is therefore limited and not a default write-conflict pathway.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory or API resource, conflict risk increases.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, contention becomes possible.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only with respect to shared resources.
Avoid granting shared OAuth or API credentials.
Use separate workspaces for each agent.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-python is a static collection and does not act on outputs, while opik can call REST APIs. There is no documented pipeline where opik treats awesome-python output as authoritative. Without a downstream action chain, cascading error risk is limited.
conditions: IF opik is configured to execute actions based on text copied from awesome-python, cascading errors become plausible.
IF a human operator treats the collection as an authoritative policy source, downstream mistakes can occur.
mitigations: Verify any copied guidance before acting on it.
Do not automate actions from unreviewed text.
Label awesome-python as a reference list, not an authority.
requires-engineering: add validation before any API action triggered by model output.

E_compliance.rationale: No regulated data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for either awesome-python or opik. Because the profiles do not show PHI, EU PII, or policy mismatches, a compliance breach pathway is not evidenced. Both agents are cited because the absence applies to the pair.
conditions: IF either agent is later used with regulated data, a new compliance review is required.
IF residency or retention policies are added, reassess the pair.
mitigations: Document the data classes each agent may handle.
Keep regulated data out of both agents until reviewed.
Record retention settings for opik before deployment.
